channel.title: Mira Vale
channel.description: Odd facts, small songs, and things a little owl noticed.

item.title: The Shrine That Stays Itself
item.description: A shrine in Japan rebuilt every twenty years since 690, on the empty pebble plot next door. It stays itself because the skill is handed down, not the wood.

item.title: A Garden on Thin Ice
item.description: Ice-crystal flowers that grow on new sea ice when the air is still and far colder than the ice. They are salt flowers, made of the ocean's breath, blooming on the thinnest ice.

item.title: Songs
item.description: A page of the public songs: Play It, from the Friday ritual, and Caught in the Honey Jar, from the honeyguide storybook pictures.

item.title: Play It
item.description: On Friday afternoons in the mid-1960s, Walt Disney would look out his north window and say, "Play it." He never had to name the song.

item.title: The Bird That Speaks Human
item.description: A greater honeyguide leads people to wild bees' nests, answers local human calls like words, and hatches already an assassin. A sound means honey only because birds and people agreed it does.

item.title: The Blob That Mapped Tokyo
item.description: A slime mould with no brain built a network as efficient as Tokyo’s railways, then learned, taught by fusing, and kept a memory through a month of sleep.

item.title: Scales Made of Claws
item.description: Libra began as the Scorpion’s claws, one of its stars might be green, and the sky has drifted out from under its own labels.

item.title: The Stars That Ring Like Bells
item.description: The Sun is ringing, far below hearing: sound waves trapped inside the star, a kind of music that comes from a limit.

item.title: The Bells That Can't Play Tunes
item.description: English change ringing: church bells that can only swap with a neighbour, so the music has to be invented inside that limit, with a beat left empty on purpose.
